poc_summary: Short summary: POC used Redwood Hosted API for 3 weeks. Goal: replace a slow keyword search flow with embedding-driven doc search + add an in-app assistant for troubleshooting. Integration: frontend calls Redwood for embeddings + chat completions. Observed user behavior: 70% short queries (<=64 tokens), 25% medium (65-512), 5% long (>512). Average prompt tokens ~95, avg completion ~55 -> avg total ~150 tokens. Latency: median token latency acceptable; p95 token-generation latency spikes during concurrent bursts. Cost sensitivity high: wants predictable unit economics for freemium -> paid rollouts.
traffic_forecast: Observed Hosted API trial metrics (week of 2025-02-02): avg QPS = 8, 95th percentile burst QPS = 22, avg concurrency ~6. Forecasted adoption after product launch: month1 avg QPS = 20, month3 avg QPS = 55, steady-state month6 avg QPS = 85, peak bursts to 200 QPS during promos. Token mix: 60% short (<64), 30% medium (64-512), 10% long (>512). Avg tokens per request forecasted 150-180. Expected monthly token volume scale: 25M -> 120M -> 320M across months 1/3/6 respectively.
capacity_sizing_notes: Initial Redwood recommendation requested: Dedicated sizing for 3-phase rollout. Rough sizing inputs from POC: 85 avg QPS steady with 2s avg generation window for long tails; target SLO p95 end-to-end <=250ms for short queries and <=700ms for medium/long (streaming ok). SE notes: baseline Dedicated (supporting burst via autoscale) estimate = 2 x A100-equivalent nodes to support 50-60 sustained QPS with healthy KV cache & batching; add autoscale pool to 6 nodes for peak bursts (~200 QPS). If using heavier models or higher output token counts, uplift to 4 baseline nodes. They asked for a more rigorous model-by-model throughput table and token-cost breakdown (SE action).
